subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this Gateway/control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and if so what is the first supported milestone?
rationale: The remaining work requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, and migration boundaries; automation cannot safely pick those product and security contracts.

options.title: Approve phased runtime split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow to execution placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the current scope and leave the broader Gateway split deferred.

options.title: Defer core architecture change
options.body: Keep supporting multi-gateway/operator workarounds and plugin or harness improvements without committing to a distributed runtime boundary yet.

recommendation.title: Approve phased runtime split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest current-main history signal on the Gateway/agent runtime docs and CLI surfaces, and also owns the worker-runtime experiment connected to the RFC.
